metadata.Description: This course is based on the first course in the CCNA curriculum. It introduces the network architectures, models, protocols, and components that enable communication among users, devices, applications, and data across modern computer networks and the Internet. Key topics include Ethernet fundamentals, IP addressing, basic network operations, and introductory network security. By the end of the course, students will be able to build and configure simple local area networks (LANs), develop appropriate IP addressing schemes, apply basic security measures, configure routers and switches, verify network connectivity, and troubleshoot common network problems. The course includes an individual Practical Examination (PE) that assesses each student’s ability to apply these skills independently. During the examination, students are required to design or complete a small network, calculate and configure IP addresses, perform basic router and switch configurations, secure network devices, verify connectivity, and identify and correct common configuration errors. The course is organized into a series of modules, each of which represents an integrated unit of learning. Every module includes instructional content, practical activities, and assessments aligned with a defined set of competencies. The scope and duration of each module vary according to the level of knowledge and practical skill required. Some modules provide foundational knowledge that supports later learning and prepares students for concepts covered in the CCNA certification examination, even where the foundational content is not assessed directly.

sections.heading: 10 LO(s)
rows: Describe the evolution of network technologies and explain how layered protocols enable communication and support end-user applications.
Students use AI and digital tools to collaborate, design, and present small network projects. The approach blends dialogue-based assessment with self-directed learning.
Apply Ethernet and switching concepts to explain and configure technologies that support efficient and reliable data transfer.
Configure switches, routers, and end devices with IP addressing and security settings to establish basic network connectivity.
Explain how physical, data link, network, and transport layers interact to enable reliable and structured data communication.
Design and implement IPv4 and IPv6 addressing schemes by calculating subnets and applying efficient address configurations in networks.
Use diagnostic tools and techniques to test and troubleshoot network connectivity, including ICMP utilities and AI-assisted methods.
Implement basic security measures by applying device hardening and configuration techniques to protect network devices and communications.
Design and implement a small network topology with routers, switches, and end devices, considering performance and scalability.
Utilize AI tools to analyze, configure, monitor, and troubleshoot networks, enhancing learning, efficiency, and network management capabilities.

sections.heading: 6 assessment(s)
rows: Practice hands-on;Dialogue-based assessment with self-directed learning.

Two assessed Lab packages are conducted under instructor guidance. Students must complete the assigned individual or group tasks, submit the required configuration files and evidence, and respond to dialogue-based questions used to verify understanding.
The lab report content can be obtained from the lab manual, or created by the instructor to align with the chapters.
Multiple choices; Marked by Computer or a suitable format

Instruction and schedules for Progress Tests must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by director of the campus. Progress test must be taken right after the last lectures of required material. Instructor has responsibility to review the test for students after graded.
CLO3, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8, CLO9 and CLO10
Practice hands-on;Dialogue-based assessment with self-directed learning.

Design, configure, secure, verify, document, and present a basic small network. Students may use approved AI tools to support planning, configuration review, troubleshooting, and documentation, but must verify all AI-generated outputs and explain their final technical decisions

Students work in groups under instructor supervision. Assessment evidence must include the network topology, addressing plan, configuration artifacts, testing results, troubleshooting records, presentation or demonstration, and individual dialogue-based assessment. Individual scores may be adjusted according to demonstrated contribution and technical understanding
The project content must incorporate the lab manuals from Modules 13 to 16, or instructor-created materials that align with those modules.
Each part of the final exam must be >=4/10 & Final Result >=5/10.
CLO2, CLO3, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7 and CLO8
Hands-on practical configuration and troubleshooting tasks in a network simulation environment
One integrated scenario consisting of several task groups

Interpret or complete a basic network topology.Calculate IPv4 subnets and assign IPv4 addresses correctly.onfigure basic IPv6 addressing when included in the approved PE blueprint.Configure switches, routers and end devices.Configure default gateways and router interfaces.Apply basic device security, including passwords, encrypted secrets, banners, SSH or login protection when required.Verify connectivity using show commands, ping, tracert/traceroute or equivalent utilities.Identify and correct common addressing, interface, gateway, VLAN, routing or security configuration errors.

The PE question bank should contain multiple equivalent variants. Network numbers, host requirements, device names and planted configuration errors should be randomized to reduce copying while maintaining equivalent difficulty.

Theoretical concepts and applied reasoning from Modules 1–16, with emphasis on protocol models, Ethernet, network and transport layers, IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, subnetting, address resolution, ICMP, application services, basic network security, small-network operation, and troubleshooting methodology.
The exam questions must be updated
